en: Impossible... I was defeated?
All right! You downed the batting center challenger! You're incredible!
Well, what's done is done. There's no use denying it.

Hey, you throw real good. I'm actually impressed. Tell me,
what's the reason behind this whole challenger thing?

It's so I could become a better pitcher. I wanted to take on
our nation's greatest batters and perfect my craft.

But I never expected to be beaten by a random stranger
in a backwater town such as this. It is clear that I require
more training.
As such, I shall be returning to the wilderness to train. Back to basics, so to speak.
...Is that really necessary?
As my parting gift, I shall leave you with this. It's for our most excellent duel. You have my thanks.
You got a <Color:8>Sturdy Katana<Color:Default>.
I shall be leaving now. Farewell!
Ahahaha! You were hardly worth my time! As stated, I'll be taking this batting center's sign.
(Damn it. I was too careless.)
...On second thought, you were a little too easy. Perhaps I should find a worthier opponent to challenge. Surely this establishment can procure one?
Oh, great! Now what are you gonna do⑬the guy's about to take the sign! You better man up, challenge him, and win next time!
Egh... Yeah, okay.
(Well, this sucks. Guess it's inevitable, though.)
Hey, it's the massage journalist guy!
Any chance you wanna show me how to hit fouls today?
Sure. I'll do it properly this time. Watch closely. I'll hit three fouls out of ten pitches.
Hope you don't eat your words again... Anyway, let's see what you got.
This sucks. Why would anyone even have to train for this?
(Oh, he must be in high school. Maybe he's got some batting trouble?)
Hey there. Why the long face?
Oh, nobody special. Just your average, uh... men's health journalist who happened to be in the area.
Oh snap! I know what that is. So do you, like, get to go to massage parlors all the time? That sounds like the best job in the world!
It's honestly not that great. I mean, I do go to get my muscle tussled quite often, but⑬ Hey, that's not what I'm here to talk about!

Look, I noticed you were talking to yourself about training.
I used to be quite the slugger myself, back in my day. If
you'd like, I'd be happy to give you some pointers.
Well... I'm just conflicted. See, my coach told me to learn how to foul pitches off.
Oh, yeah. He wants you to learn how to cut away pitches you don't like and run up the pitch count.
Yeah, well. I'm our team's cleanup hitter, but my stats after two strikes are terrible.
I get psyched out by the pitcher, I swing at bad throws, and I have a pile of strikeouts to show for it.
Coach has had enough, and he's talking about dropping me from the starting lineup unless I can get it together.
So that's why he wants you to learn how to hit fouls. He's not wrong, you know.
When a batter gets behind on the count, his ability to foul off pitches really makes a difference.
For instance, if you have two strikes against, being able to foul off the pitcher's best throws will annoy him while you wait for a chance.
I can understand that, but it seems so cheesy. It's tough to get into that mindset.
What's tough about it? Cutting fouls takes a lot of technique. You have to be an expert at controlling your swing.
Think about batting like a chess match between you and the pitcher. Your cutting technique is just another tool in your arsenal.
By fouling off pitches, you can negate the pitcher's best stuff and narrow down his pitching choices. Which puts pressure on the guy.
You could say that having the ability to cut makes a batter all the more dangerous.
Oh. I get it now. That's why. But how am I supposed to learn how to cut?
This might be an oversimplification, but I try to draw a bead on the ball, and swing a split second early. It's like jumping the gun.
Could I maybe get you to give me a demonstration?
Hmm, I suppose I could do that. Just watch, I'll hit three fouls out of ten throws.
That would be great! Thank you!
Wow! That was an eye-opener.
Heh. Hope so.
I think I can do this now. Thank you! Please, take this.
Go for it, guy. Once you master it, you'll be much tougher to pitch against.
That's right! I'm gonna do it!
(Heh, well that sure brings back memories. Hope I wasn't too preachy.)
Huh? Weren't you going to foul off three pitches?
I, uh... kind of screwed it up there.
Oh, I see how it is. You're one of those old guys who give all kinds of advice that they themselves don't follow. Well, that's disappointing.
(Urgh... I don't even have a comeback!)
Oh, you're back.
Oh, yeah. You haven't gone in for your surgery yet?
No... If the surgery fails, I'll never be able to hold my bat again. Even the thought of that terrifies me.
All right, let's have another bet. This time, I'll hit a homer within the first three pitches for sure. If I do that, you go get that surgery. Okay?
Sounds good. Challenge accepted.
Um, excuse me.
You're the guy from Kotetsu-san's blog, aren't you? The awesome batter?
Yeah, I guess that's me. But what's up with you? Are you an inpatient or something?
Yes. I'm due for an operation. But I got scared and ran away from the hospital.
I kept thinking about what would happen if it didn't work, and I couldn't go through with it.
The surgery's that critical?
The doctor says there's nothing to worry about. But I'm the one going under the knife. Either they succeed or they fail. Fifty-fifty.
If the operation fails, I'll never be able to hold my bat again.
When I thought of that, I found myself running here.
And then I saw you, the hero of the local batting cages. I'm sorry, though, I shouldn't have bothered you.
Ah, it's okay. You're not bothering me any. But listen, you can't avoid this surgery, can you? Shouldn't you be going back to the hospital?
I know I should, but... Urk... I'm scared out of my wits!
If I could, I'd rather put off the surgery until it's too late to operate!
Whoa, you don't want to do that.
I try not to think about it, but I keep dwelling on what would happen if they screw up.
Argh! Why do I have to go through this!?
Urk... *snivel*
How about we do this? We'll have a little bet, you and me.
A bet?
I'll go into this batting cage here. If I hit a homer, you go get your surgery. Deal?
Wasn't there a story like that from the big leagues? Some famous slugger promised a homer to a sick little boy?
Yeah, there was. Now I'm not claiming to be anyone famous, but what do you say? Do we have a deal?
I'll even limit myself to just the first three pitches.
Only three pitches?
Well, it's a home run at a batting center. If I get too many throws, it'll be too easy, right?
Okay. I accept that challenge.
That's settled, then. Just watch me, all right?
(I'll look like a chump if I don't come through. It's either a homer or nothing.)
You did it! It's a home run! You really hit a home run for me!
Yup. Now it's on you to hold up your end of the bargain. The doctors are waiting to operate on you, aren't they?
Okay. I'm not scared anymore. I'll go have it done. Time to get circumcised.
Huh? Did you say... circumcised?
Yes, it's a very delicate operation. If they screw up, it would be disastrous. For example...
You won't be able to hold your bat anymore?
What the crap? <Italic>That</Italic> bat!?
Eheheh.
"Eheheh"? You little dingbat! Go get it snipped already! You got me all worked up over nothing.
I'm ready to take this on now. Please take this as my thanks. Really, thank you so much!
Oh, no. I won the bet.
Uh, yeah. Sorry, kid. I made it harder for you to get that surgery.
Oh, no, it's okay, really. I don't think I should be getting that surgery after all.
Well, if it isn't Shinada himself.
Been awhile, hasn't it? You do remember me, don't you?
Wait... Ashida-san?
Heh, glad you didn't forget. After all these years, too.
I could never. Anyway, what brings you here?
My son found a photo of you online, and it led to a popular baseball blog. After reading up on it, I learned I might run into you here.
(Must be Kotetsu's blog.)
The internet's mighty useful, isn't it?
Ashida-san, are you still a batting pitcher with the Wyverns?
No, I gave that up. I'm past fifty now. How about you? Growing old gracefully?
Well, I'm growing old, at least.
I pitched to you for the four years you were on the farm⑬any of that still fresh in your head?
Of course! I pretty much learned how to bat from your pitching.
You believed in me a lot more than our batting coach did...
Well, I'm glad you're still active. Whoever made that website I mentioned keeps ranting and raving about you.
That's just him frothing at the mouth. All I do is come here for a little practice.
Heh, a batter of your caliber loose among the crowd? No wonder you gained a reputation.
Either way, it's good to see you haven't lost your passion for the game.
Hah, you think? I wish I could agree with confidence.
That so? Huh. In my case, I still have regrets.
Mm. In spite of just being a batting pitcher, I loved my career with the Wyverns.
Due to my age, I thought my body was telling me to retire. But when I saw you slugging away on that blog, I realized how much I missed the game.
I'm saying I want to get back to pitching for a living. To get back into the league, educate young players, and help them grow.
Old fogey that I am, I must have something left to contribute.
Okay. Then why did you come see me?
I came to you for help, Shinada. I want you to gauge whether I still have what it takes to do my job.
And you want me for that?
'Course I do. A batting pitcher's gotta pitch in a way that batters can hit⑬which is surprisingly difficult.

Takes even more control than a major league knuckleballer.
My role in this is to help batters gain confidence as they
overcome whatever pitches they find challenging.
Yeah, and I'm living proof. I got off the farm thanks to you. Sure took me long enough...
Then, will you help me? It won't take much. Should be a one-and-done job.
What would you like me to do?
I'm gonna take the mound for ten pitches. All you need to do is hit them.
So it's a ten-pitch duel, then?
Yes and no. I'm pitching to let you hit, not get you out. That's my job as a batting pitcher.
What if I can't hit anything?
Then I'll take it as a sign that I've worn out my welcome as a batting pitcher. I'll draw the curtains on my career and never pitch again.
Whoa, you're really gonna make that huge decision on ten pitches?
Yeah, pretty much. It's all riding on you, Shinada.
But you know I retired a long time ago. Even if your pitching is good, what if I totally suck?
It's my job to determine the batter's ability and throw what they can hit. If I can't do that, I'm no longer useful.
I mean, I see your point, but...
Look, it's you who made me regret leaving the game. So I'm holding you accountable.
...If that's how it is, then okay. Pitch me up.
Good, this is what we'll do: I'll throw ten pitches, and if I have any hope of resuming my career, you should be able to hit at least eight of them.
Eight out of ten? That's a pretty tall order.
Like I said, I'm not trying to get you out. I'm throwing to let you hit. There's nothing challenging about it.
Into the cage you go, Shinada. Come on, this should be fun for you.
(What an odd challenge. But I have to hit these for Ashida-san's sake.)
There! You did great, Ashida-san. You still have your control.
Thanks, Shinada. Heh, it's an odd thing, having a batter pump the confidence of a pitcher.
Can't say I've ever done that before.
Of course, there's no guarantee the team will even be interested in rehiring me. But you gave me the confidence to try.
It's all thanks to you, Shinada. This is a token of my appreciation. Accept it, if you would.
Your batting hasn't eroded one bit. I think you could still make it in the pros today. You could even take Sawada if you wanted.

Ehehe. Remember, I'm banned from the big leagues for life.
Appreciate the compliment, though.
Yeah, well, I don't care what the others say. I never doubted your innocence in the least. You'd never steal a sign.
That home run was all you. I threw to you for four years. I know what you can do.
You were the only person who ever vouched for me. Back then, and even now.
But I had no influence. I couldn't save you.
Sorry. I'm sure you didn't want to hear that now.
